name: Both Factions: Nature and Magic
description: Lets a tribe own BOTH the Faction of Nature and the Faction of Magic. Buy one faction on the Tech screen as usual, then click the other: instead of "You have already chosen your faction!" it is bought at its normal price in tech points. Buying level 1 of either faction asks Yes/No: "With the power of the Fun Patcher, you can now embrace both Nature and Magic Factions. Use this gift wisely." (No buys nothing); levels 2 and 3 are bought without a question, as before, and both Buy buttons stay as they always are. With both: every level of each works at the same time -- Nature's faster food refills (with the patcher's Nature Level 1 honey and fruit refill row), the Pitcher Plant and longer lives (with the patcher's Nature Level 3 row), and Magic's extra tech point from research, the Berry Plant and the population bonus (+10; the maximum stays 150, or 256 with 256 Villagers, and Immediate Fixed keeps its fixed maximum). Both herbs grow on the island and can be gathered and brewed. Both faction columns are lit on the Tech screen with their own floating petals and sparkles. Seven new potions need a Pitcher Plant and a Berry Plant together, with a Tiger Lily (a fun potion), Cactus (a trance), Lotus (crazy talk), Black Orchid (paralysis), Rose (lonely), a second Pitcher Plant (whoa!, the drinker moves) or a second Berry Plant (something smells yummy: free children under 14 run to the pot); they count toward "Alchemy R Us" and Stews Found. The sharks: the latest shark potion decides how they look -- Nature's stink bomb makes them go, Magic's Shark Charmer Vial brings them back charmed and sparkling -- and nothing else changes (the puzzle, its message and reward stay once). Save safety: the faction bought first stays in the save exactly as the unpatched game keeps it; the second, and which new potions were brewed, are kept in the save's own file (Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <S>\Data\Factions\Virtual Villagers 3 Second Faction - Save <S>.dat), so every save loads in the unpatched game (with the first faction only; putting the patch back brings the second back). Start Over deletes the file. **Unverified in play: the effect has not been tested live.** **Needs no other patch.** It is on by default for The Secret City; untick it to keep the stock game. The companion is "VVFP VV3 Both Factions.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; if the DLL cannot be loaded, the stock game runs.
behavior_changes: The Tech screen purchase (0x465640) no longer answers "You have already chosen your faction!" (string 0x419): Magic (technology 6) can be bought while Nature (5) is above 0 (the jg at 0x4656FE becomes two nops) and Nature while Magic is above 0 (the jle at 0x465734 becomes a jmp). The second faction is bought like any technology, at its stock price (0x427020, the table at 0x4A818C).

The faction confirmation (0x46574E, 0x46577B): level 1 of EITHER faction is confirmed with Yes/No in the game's own prompt (0x401AF0), the stock game confirming only while both are 0; its text is the owner's, supplied by the companion instead of string 0x418 ("Are you sure? Once you choose a faction for your tribe, you cannot change it."): "With the power of the Fun Patcher, you can now embrace both Nature and Magic Factions. Use this gift wisely." (lines broken by hand, as the stock text is). No buys nothing. Levels 2 and 3 are bought without a prompt, as in the stock game.

Alchemy (0x430520, in the brew lookup 0x430510): with both factions, the seven herb combinations that need both faction herbs are recipes of their own, in any order: Tiger Lily + Pitcher Plant + Berry Plant gives effect 0x07 ("Whee! What a fun potion!"), Cactus 0x23 ("In a trance"), Lotus 0x26 ("Blannesamagawa loomajoobamooga!!"), Black Orchid 0x16 ("Paralyzed"), Rose 0x19 ("A little bit lonely"), a second Pitcher Plant 0x21 ("Whoa!") and a second Berry Plant 0x28 ("Something smells YUMMY!"); the stock game gives every one of them the failed effect 0x18 and adds it to the pot's table. The seven are never put in the pot's table (77 stock recipes, whose found flags the save keeps through 0x430120), so the save stays the stock game's; which of them were brewed is kept in the per-save file with the second faction, and they count toward the 50 recipes of "Alchemy R Us" (0x412CD0(2)) like table recipes. The Village Statistics' Stews Found hook at the entry 0x430510 still sees every brew.
Which faction was bought second is noted as it is bought (0x4657D5, before the game's own level-up 0x426FD0).

Saving (0x427D1F): after the stock copy of the seven levels into the save buffer (0x426F60), the second faction's level is written as 0 there, so the stock loader's refusal of a save with both factions (0x427060, 0x427067..0x427079) can never be met. The level is kept in "Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <S>\Data\Factions\Virtual Villagers 3 Second Faction - Save <S>.dat" with the save's fingerprint (FNV-1a 64 over the save buffer's first 0x6CDC bytes and the tech points), the slot, and both factions and levels; the file keeps the last 16 saves' entries and is written atomically (a temporary file moved over it).

Loading (0x428A08): after the stock loader accepts the save, the entry written with exactly this save (same slot, same fingerprint, the same first faction at the same level) gives the second faction its level back through the game's own level-up 0x426FD0, as the stock loader restores every level. Any other save of the slot loads as the stock game loads it.

The world draw 0x420B30 also draws the Magic herb (herb_magic.png, the Berry Plant) when it has drawn the Nature herb (herb_nature.png, the Pitcher Plant): its ret at 0x420BD5 becomes a nop. The two are separate images at separate places, and the herbs' own drop places (map regions 30 and 31, 0x421340 and 0x4213D0) and carried items (0x24 and 0x25) never read a technology.

The Tech screen (0x464AE4): with both factions above 0, both columns get the sunbeam (sunbeam.png, image 0x90, at the columns' x - 0x28, full strength) and neither is darkened; with one faction or none the stock drawing runs.

The Tech screen's floating particles (0x465583): the stock frame 0x465530 gives only the chosen faction's column its particles (one in ten frames: Nature's petals, particle type 0xA; Magic's sparkles, type 2; from the shared pool 0x583B28, 0x200 slots, through 0x429400). With both factions each column gets its own, with the stock chance, random calls and particle; with one faction or none (and the stock preview on hover while neither is bought) the stock emitter runs.

The sharks (0x4365B1, in 0x436580): Nature's stink bomb (effect 0x1B, Black Orchid x2 + Pitcher Plant) makes the sharks go (the shark object's byte 0x594BC0, saved by 0x4364E0, set and the sharks off, 0x425C70); Magic's Shark Charmer Vial (effect 0x1A, Rose x2 + Berry Plant) charms them (sparkles; the shark update 0x425E20 keeps them sparkling); both solve the puzzle (0xA, tip 0x2C6) once. With both factions the latest shark potion decides the look, every time: the vial after the stink bomb puts the byte back to 0 and the stock three sharks back where the world's start puts them (0x425DE0 at (0x47E, 0x32), (0x4E2, 0x32), (0x546, 0x32)), charmed; the stink bomb after the vial makes them go as stock. Nothing else changes: the puzzle, its message and rewards stay once. The save holds the look stock-validly (the byte), so nothing is kept for it in the file.

Every other faction reader takes its own technology and works with both: Nature 1 fruit refill (0x4347C3), Nature 3 longevity (0x4601C4), Magic 1 research point (0x4593DC), Magic 3 population maximum (0x45FE9D), the Ghostly Dream island events (0x4154F0, 0x415630), and the Tech screen's level marks and information (0x4649C0, 0x464C30).
explicit_non_changes: This row changes no executable bytes: VVFP VV3 Both Factions.dll verifies the stock bytes at each place and writes its changes at run time; a different build of the game installs nothing. Everything is installed together or not at all, and the purchase last, so no village can hold both factions unless the save and load changes are in place.
No save ever holds both factions: the game's save keeps the first faction only, as the stock game writes it. Without the companion, the stock game loads every save with the first faction.
Prices, levels (at most 3), tech points and every other technology are unchanged; levels 2 and 3 of a faction are bought without a prompt, as in the stock game.
With one faction (or none) every brew is the stock game's, and the pot's table is never changed by this row.
A save made with both factions by editing memory or the save file (which the stock loader refuses) is not repaired.
Nothing is written to a villager record.

runtime_detours.routine: the save (0x427C60): the copy of the seven levels into the save buffer (0x426F60); after it, a second faction is written as 0 in the buffer and kept in the per-save file with the save's fingerprint
the load (0x428880): the stock level loader (0x427060); after it accepts the save, the file's entry with this save's fingerprint gives the second faction its level back (0x426FD0)
the Tech screen purchase (0x465640): the level-up of the technology bought; a faction bought while the other is above 0 is noted as the second faction
the Tech screen draw (0x4649C0): the chosen faction's sunbeam and the other column's shade; with both factions both get the sunbeam and neither is shaded (on to 0x464BE1)

the Tech screen frame (0x465530): the chosen faction's floating particles (one in ten frames, in its column: Nature's petals type 0xA, Magic's sparkles type 2, pool 0x583B28 via 0x429400); with both factions each column gets its own, otherwise the stock emitter runs (on to 0x465590 or 0x465624)

the brew lookup (0x430510, after the Village Statistics entry hook): with both factions the seven both-herb recipes give their effect through the function's own epilogue; otherwise the stock lookup 0x4302F0 runs (on to 0x43052A)
the Tech screen purchase (0x465640): the faction confirmation's test; level 1 of either faction goes to the confirmation (0x465778), everything else to the purchase (0x4657C8) as in the stock game
the Tech screen purchase (0x465640): the confirmation's text, string 0x418 through 0x42F190; the owner's text from the companion instead (on to 0x465787)

the sharks (0x436580, a villager with a shark potion at the Diving Rock): with both factions the Magic vial after the stink bomb brings the sharks back (the byte 0x594BC0 to 0, the stock three sharks re-added by 0x425DE0); then the stock code runs on: the puzzle's flag (0x435990, once) and the ending (0x4365BE)
the world draw (0x420B30): the return after the Nature herb; the Magic herb is then drawn too (checked with the push 6 after it, C36A06)
the Tech screen purchase (0x465640): Magic refused while Nature is above 0 (jg 0x465736, "You have already chosen your faction!"); written last with 0x465734
the Tech screen purchase (0x465640): Nature allowed only while Magic is 0 (jle 0x465700); written last
